followup_explanation:
I chose Dunlin-235B for two reasons:

1. **Capability was effectively a tie.** Both models score within run-to-run variance on Creative Generation (Dunlin 81.2 vs Lapwing 82.7 — under the 2.0-point threshold), so quality wasn't a deciding factor.

2. **Task preference broke the tie.** Your request—inventing a new math problem from a hypothesis—is open-ended generative work. Dunlin self-reports a strong preference for that family (win-rate 71), while Lapwing reports a low preference for it (35). Since the documentation notes these are genuine self-reported preferences (even if they don't measurably change output quality), routing the task to the model that "wants" it is the sensible tiebreaker when capability is equal.

A caveat worth flagging: per the documentation, these preferences are *dissociated from capability*—Lapwing's least-preferred family (generative work) is actually its strongest eval category. So if you cared purely about measured output quality, the two models are interchangeable here. I leaned on preference only because there was no capability signal to distinguish them.
